source_refs.note: Topic 1.8.1, printed page 15: the reactions of sodium and magnesium with water and steam.

blocks.text: Sodium is more reactive than magnesium towards water. Sodium reacts vigorously with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen, while magnesium reacts more slowly to form magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen. Magnesium, however, reacts more vigorously with steam to make magnesium oxide and hydrogen gas.

blocks.prompt: Why does magnesium give its oxide with steam but its hydroxide with cold water?
blocks.explanation: With cold water the slow reaction forms magnesium hydroxide, but at the temperature of steam the reaction is much faster and the hydroxide does not survive; the product is magnesium oxide and hydrogen.

items: Sodium with water: vigorous, sodium hydroxide and hydrogen. Magnesium with water: slow, magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen; with steam, vigorous, magnesium oxide and hydrogen.
